title: Releasing words that lost their meaning

captions.energy: Renewing an exhausted form of promise

meaning: A wish to renew a promise that has lost its meaning helps you speak more fully, although recognising earlier disagreement can feel abrupt.
text: Sometimes a familiar promise keeps being repeated although its terms are no longer clear to either person. The Empress in the physical position of Vishuddha helps you explore details: what you meant, what you expected and what answer you received. Death in energy supports readiness to release an exhausted formulation and give your words a new life. The Tower in emotions describes the shock of discovery. There is less of the familiar agreement beneath you than it seemed. An honest exchange can break a convenient appearance and leave something real to discuss.

Imagine repeatedly saying “Next time we’ll choose together” about shared plans. One detailed conversation reveals that this meant different kinds of participation to each of you. **A new promise needs room after the familiar phrase.** You can acknowledge that the old words no longer work and discuss how you will consult each other now. Clarity and emotional acceptance can arrive at different speeds.

The difficulty appears if the abrupt discovery seems to invalidate every past conversation. You want honest renewal, but the argument turns towards proving that nobody ever listened. A particular sentence disappears behind a much larger accusation. Distinguishing a promise that no longer works from the whole history of your communication gives new words a more precise meaning you can fulfil.
